60 gpm was drilled into the lower sub-Robinson units in the valley of Spring Creek along the eastern part of Tract II. The yield of this well indicates that the lower sub-Robinson units are capable of yielding moderate amounts of water.
Recharge to this unit is vertically from overlying rocks and laterally from the west and south of Tracts II and III (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 1, p. 42). Discharge is to springs where the unit crops out, to lower aquifers, and (near the end of the flow system) upward to overlying aquifers.
Deeper Aquifers - Deeper aquifers which do not crop out in the project area are little used as a source of ground water (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 1, p. 22). The source (or yield) zones have been identified for 156 wells inventoried in the project area. Only 6 of these derived their water from below the undifferentiated Fort Union aquifer. Five of these apparently drew water from the Tullock-Hell Creek aquifer. In the project area, Westmoreland drilled three test holes from 90 to 180 feet into the Tullock Member, attempting to develop an adequate water supply for the mining operation, but an insufficient supply of water was obtained (U.S. Bureau of Indian Affairs, 1974, p. 87). The other deep well which taps an aquifer below the Fort Union undifferentiated aquifer is Westmoreland's 7,977 foot well to the Mission Canyon Member of the Madison Limestone. It has a potentiometric head of 175 feet above ground surface. A 9,336 foot deep well at Colstrip, Montana, (20 miles east of the project area) produces from the Madison Limestone and the Red River Formation and has a potentiometric head 460 feet above ground surface (Westmoreland Resources 1975 1, p 20, 21).
